note: Per-subsystem judgment on why it carries host guards (isTauri / isHeadlessHost / usePlatform). Produced by `pnpm audit:host-parity:report` and classified by hand — the census is mechanical, the classification is not. `confidence: "low"` marks a row decided from naming and a spot check rather than a full read; those are where a reviewer should look first. Classifications: physically-impossible (the host genuinely lacks the surface), unmigrated (no physical reason — the work just was not done), ui-assumption (backend can reach parity; the UI keys off the host instead of a capability), seam-infrastructure (this IS the host-detection/transport layer; branching on host is its job).

app/me.note: One `usePlatform()` in page.tsx feeds `isMeEntryOffered` (components/mobile/me/me-entries.ts): on `tauri` every host-operation-gated entry is offered unchecked, elsewhere only when the paired host's runtime snapshot advertises the route's operation. The desktop half should read the same snapshot.

components/account.note: `usePlatform()` in account-lock-screen.tsx only picks the runtime badge text (OS keychain, mobile secure storage, Browser Vault). Unlocking is the same on every host.

components/automation.note: The consent overlay hides itself off-Tauri; once consent is remotable it should key off the capability instead.

components/boot.note: `usePlatform()` in boot-screen.tsx to pick the shell-appropriate boot presentation. A brain has no boot screen.

components/browser.note: Already degrades to RemoteBrowserPreview / iframe off-Tauri, and headless has the full browser.remote surface (28 ops). The guard should follow the capability.

components/connectivity.note: add-host-form selects mDNS versus loopback discovery from isTauri(); paired-step uses usePlatform for mobile local-profile fallback and sign-out platform context. Pairing itself already uses the shared host registry and transports.

components/desktop.note: Native window/menu chrome. Some children may be ui-assumption; split when paying down.

components/devices.note: Device controls and ownership candidates must be selected from runtime capabilities; the current guards still key presentation and grant affordances directly off the shell.

components/filespace.note: `isTauri()` in conversation-files-panel.tsx picks the copied link format: a `cognia://session/…?view=files` deep link on the desktop, a web URL elsewhere. It gates no files behaviour.

components/global-search.note: `usePlatform()` in the dialog for platform-appropriate chrome and shortcut hints (ADR-0129).

components/inbox.note: Adapter health/consent affordances gated on isTauri(); the connector runtime itself works headless.

components/pet.note: The in-page pet renders anywhere; only the overlay window is desktop-bound.

components/remote-desktop.note: remote-desktop-viewer-page.tsx: `access === "web-console"` embeds RemoteConsoleView, a native child webview over the page that needs Tauri's multi-webview; a link without a remote host needs a Host of the renderer's own. Every other shell falls back to LaunchNotice (open externally).

components/runtime.note: `usePlatform()` in surface-availability-boundary.tsx goes to `resolveRuntimeRecovery` to pick per-shell recovery copy and actions. Availability itself comes from the runtime snapshot; the platform only changes the remedy shown.

components/selection-toolbar.note: ADR-0093/0095 — needs a visible desktop and screen-recording permission.

components/settings.note: 145 guards / 93 files — the largest single cluster, and 21 sections are hard-marked `desktopOnly: true`. This is the primary target of the `desktopOnly → requires: [capability]` migration.

components/thread-handoff.note: handed-off-banner and thread-handoff-source-dialog pass `isDesktop: isTauri()` to continueOnHostRefusal/bringBackRefusal (lib/remote-host/code-supply), which refuse with "not-desktop": the source side snapshots this machine's working tree and issues a host-admin lease from this desktop. A phone or browser holds no working tree to hand over or bring back.

components/ui.note: `usePlatform()` in loading-states.tsx to fold host-specific boot phases (pairing, host, sync) into one timeline. Presentation only; components/ui is otherwise the untested shadcn tree.

components/workspace.note: One `isTauri()` in workspace-picker-list.tsx, and it is half right: the desktop opens a native folder dialog, while a paired phone or browser opens the HOST's tree through `fs_list_workspace_dir`. The capability half of that decision is already the gate (`gate("fs_list_workspace_dir").available`); the `isTauri()` beside it stands in for "can I show a native dialog", which is a UI question keyed off the host rather than off a capability. Only an unpaired browser genuinely has neither path.

hooks/agents.note: `isTauri()` in use-agent-actions.ts picks how an exported character pack is saved: native save dialog plus plugin-fs write on the desktop, a Blob download elsewhere. Same body either way.

hooks/automation.note: use-automation-host-status reads this desktop's AX / screen-recording / UIA permissions and native automation capabilities (ADR-0020). use-session-sandbox-desktop passes `isTauri()` as `lifecycleHostAvailable`, offering the sandbox GUI viewer only on the desktop: that half is a ui-assumption to split out when paying down.

hooks/connectivity.note: use-remote-access selects localTransport on Tauri for companion_signaling_status, otherwise the current transport. This makes desktop settings inspect their local host instead of an active remote workspace.

hooks/devices.note: Device discovery and grant actions currently branch on Tauri even though Companion and remote-host transports expose capability-based equivalents.

hooks/glance.note: use-glance-quota gates vault enumeration, local-login discovery and per-account limit refresh on `isTauri()` because the subscription vault is a Tauri command family. A brain's subscription accounts and quotas are host-neutral data; this follows lib/subscription. The tray glance windows themselves are physical (lib/tauri/glance.ts).

hooks/global-search.note: `isTauri()` around the open-folder and check-updates palette actions, each falling back to a localized "desktop only" toast rather than failing silently, plus one `usePlatform()` for context assembly. Honest degradation, not a hidden gap.

hooks/goal.note: use-goal-controls, use-goal-create and use-goal-verifier-options read `usePlatform() === "mobile"` as "remote" (writes through the paired host's control grant, verifier catalog from the host). A browser paired to a cloud host is also remote but reads as local and writes its own Dexie; the decision should key off the runtime snapshot's target.

hooks/pet.note: `usePlatform()` in use-pet-console-mode feeds resolvePetAvailability for the local pet overlay window (ADR-0058). Remote care is already decided by the active host's `pet.remote-care` capability.

hooks/prompts.note: use-effective-chat-preview reports project instructions as `omitted: "no-filesystem"` off Tauri. A turn sent from a paired client runs on a host that has a filesystem, so the preview misstates what the run gets; it should ask the execution host or follow its capability.

hooks/sandbox.note: use-project-runtime-environment reports portsAvailable and allows openPort only on Tauri. Environment port RPCs exist on the companion plane; the renderer still keys availability on the shell rather than the selected host capability.

hooks/sites.note: `use-site-action-gate.ts` reads `usePlatform()` to disable host-privileged Sites controls outside Tauri, and its own docblock names why the boundary is physical: builds run through `sandbox_exec`, previews spawn a PTY, provider tokens need the OS keyring, and the manifest lives on disk. Getting it wrong is worse than an error, because the keyring silently falls back to an in-memory store and a saved token would look accepted and vanish. The console renders on every host and disables with a reason rather than blanking, which is the shape this classification asks for.

hooks/squads.note: `usePlatform()` in use-squad-templates maps the shell to a TemplatePlatform that applySquadTemplate uses to filter template compatibility. Catalog filtering, not a backend restriction.

hooks/terminal.note: Two guards. `use-ssh-host-key-change.tsx` gates TRUSTING a changed host key on `isTauri()`, because the known-hosts file it would write lives on the machine running the SSH client, and its comment says so. `use-terminal-autocomplete.ts` passes `detectPlatform()` as data for path-shape completion, which is a fact about the host being completed against rather than a branch.

lib/account-sync.note: enrollment/platform.ts `currentDevicePlatform()` maps the shell to the registry's DevicePlatform recorded at enrollment; naming the device kind is its job. The headless brain enrolls through cli/src/account-sync and never calls it.

lib/automation.note: AX/UIA against a real desktop. Consent is NOT in this category — see ADR-0059: it routes to a paired device via notifications.remote.

lib/background-tasks.note: redispatch.ts reads Claude settings hooks through `readClaudeEffectiveSettings` only on `isTauri()`. On a brain `nativeLifecycleHooks` stays "uninspected-host", so every recovery record is stamped non-idempotent and auto-resume is more conservative than needed. Reading the brain's own settings is host-neutral work behind the Tauri-only lib/claude/settings path; it degrades safely but is not physical.

lib/best-of-n.note: projection.ts `canManageBestOfNRuns()` is `isTauri() && !isRemoteHostActive()`, so a headless brain, itself the executing host, is cast as a `pairedObserver` and team-api / the /best-of-n action refuse to start or manage runs. The best_of_n_* arms are host-neutral (rpc/filesystem.rs → cognia_task_workspace_host); the guard hides work the brain could do.

lib/browser.note: `installSnapshotInvalidation` gates on `isTauri()` because the snapshot-dirty event arrives on the Tauri event plane. The code already degrades honestly (the cache stays conservative and `fresh` bypasses it), so this is a missed optimisation on a cloud host rather than a broken feature — it clears when the browser events move onto the swappable seam.

lib/browser-companion.note: host-transport.ts picks how this process reaches its own `/ws/browser-companion` sockets: localTransport on the desktop, the brain's service-plane transport headless, nothing on a phone or tab (`hostServesBrowserSockets`). Both hosts are complete.

lib/browser/local-client.ts.note: Only the screencast frame stream uses Tauri IPC directly: `browser_local_frames_subscribe` passes a `Channel` that Rust fills with raw ArrayBuffers (InvokeResponseBody::Raw), and its paired unsubscribe. The Transport contract has no per-call binary channel. The family is client.local (the local Chromium on this desktop); remote hosts stream through browser.remote instead. Every other call here goes through `transport`.

lib/connectors.note: installConnectorRuntime gates on isTauri() and the brain bypasses it with skipHostGate. The transports themselves are migrated: all nine IM adapters subscribe through `connectorListen` (lib/connectors/events.ts), which is the only production file here importing @tauri-apps/api/event and is a declared SEAM_OWNER — so the four IM platforms that once could not receive on a cloud host now can. What remains is the bootstrap gate itself.

lib/devices.note: pair-entry.ts sends "Pair a device" to Settings → Companion (native QR) on the desktop and to the surface contract's standalone remedy route elsewhere. Navigation only.

lib/docs-providers.note: This IS the host-support declaration for the cloud-document providers. `listAvailableDocsProviders` and `isDocsProviderHostSupported` filter a registry by each provider's own `hosts` list, which is the registry's job and the reason a mobile user sees WHY a provider is missing instead of an empty picker. The one `isTauri()` outside that, in `providers/google/http.ts`, picks the Tauri transport over `fetch` and is the same seam question.

lib/files-library.note: workspace-files-io `hasLocalWorkspaceFiles()` returns `isTauri()`: only the desktop renderer lists its own task-workspace ledger, and a paired device shows the host's. The ledger (cognia-task-workspace resource_index) is host-neutral; the guard answers "is this renderer co-located with a ledger" by shell rather than capability.

lib/filespace.note: grants-client `fileShareTransport()` pins the desktop's own file-share host to localTransport so it never follows a selected remote host, and routes everything else through `transport`; the brain passes its transport through FileShareTarget. Both hosts serve the file_* surface.

lib/gateway.note: mint-session-ticket `prepareExternalAgentGatewayRoute` sends a headless brain to `prepareHostGatewayRoute` (a host task lease, credentials from the host-owned snapshot); the desktop builds the route from renderer settings and subscription credentials. Both hosts work: the guard marks two credential authorities ADR-0250 phase 2 should collapse onto the host-owned path.

lib/git.note: The git RPC arms carry NO host gate at all — they are host-neutral and work headless today. host-feature-manifest.ts still declares source-control.git as tauri-only (class E finding).

lib/global-search.note: headless-context records detectPlatform/isTauri and derives canBrowseHostFolders from isTauri while clearing UI-only navigation state. Host-folder browsing availability should eventually follow the execution host capability, not the renderer platform.

lib/host-secrets.note: provider-key-overlay `defaultHostProviderKeyDeps()` loads sealed provider keys from each host's own store: service-plane `transport` on a brain, the desktop's own command and event on Tauri (never the routed transport), none elsewhere. Equivalent by construction.

lib/island.note: client emitToWindow/listenHere guard Tauri inter-window events for the local island overlay. A headless process has no desktop overlay window to receive or display these events.

lib/keyring.note: Branches to the OS keyring on desktop and an AES-GCM IndexedDB blob elsewhere; headless uses cognia-secrets. Equivalent by construction, not a gap.

lib/magpie.note: client.ts reads the Magpie gateway port with `magpie_gateway_port` only on `isTauri()` and otherwise assumes 3425. The port comes from the tauri-free cognia_ccswitch::magpie behind a desktop-only command, so a brain probing its own machine gets the default instead of the configured port. Follows lib/ccswitch.

lib/mcp.note: run-server-map `buildRunMcpServerMap` injects OAuth bearer headers and refresh for remote MCP servers only on `isTauri()`; brain-run turns (build-options, ACP children) resolve SecretRefs only. Headless already serves `mcp_oauth_load_entry`, so OAuth-protected MCP servers fail on brain runs for no physical reason.

lib/native/codex-app-dispatch.ts.note: Drives the installed Codex DESKTOP app, not a service. `cognia-codex-app` resolves `~/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock` (`codex_home()`), and when that socket is absent `connect_or_launch` recovers by opening `codex://threads/new` through the OS URL-scheme handler — a container has neither the app nor a handler to register the scheme. Same footing as AX/UIA: the SUBJECT is missing, not the plumbing. Note the plumbing is in fact host-neutral (`run_cdp_control` shells a Node sidecar), so do not 'fix' this by making the sidecar host-agnostic — the socket still never appears. Reclassified 2026-08-16; the 2026-08-15 audit's "no physical reason found" was wrong.

lib/ocr.note: Only apple-vision and windows-media-ocr are physical; packages/ocr/src/registry.ts already subtracts exactly those two for headless. tesseract/ocrs/paddle run anywhere.

lib/platform.note: detect.ts + capabilities.ts + host-feature-manifest.ts — the tables themselves.

lib/plugin.note: The clearest case in the repo: rpc/plugins.rs has 52 headless-only arms and 12 desktop-only ones. The subsystem is split in half with neither side complete.

lib/power.note: screen-wake-lock selects native power_screen_holds_set on Tauri or the browser Screen Wake Lock API elsewhere. Availability is native support or the actual browser request method; acquisition failures do not mark holds as active.

lib/remote-desktop.note: launch.ts `remoteDesktopClientKind()` picks desktop/phone/web to choose the launch mechanism (app-link open, native phone handoff or in-app browser, tab). Client presentation of one launch decision.

lib/reply-copilot.note: screen/overlay-client guards the local nonactivating chat-copilot desktop window, its placement and inter-window events. Clipboard writes have a browser fallback; the guarded overlay requires a visible OS desktop.

lib/router-fusion.note: verify/acceptance-profiles defaults onWeb to !isTauri before evaluating workspace trust. The host is injectable, but a headless host should not inherently be treated as a browser; this remains a default-host capability migration.

lib/sandbox.note: Reversed asymmetry: `isHeadlessHost()` enables always-on-Host behaviour the desktop lacks: the container shell tier (container-exec-adapter → service-only `environment_task_shell_exec`, an ungated arm), dispatched-agent placement (host-agent-placement) and scratch workspaces (task-shell-placement). A desktop in host mode has no physical reason to go without them. delivery-source-hosts additionally pins local vs remote transport for cleanup, which is seam work.

lib/sftp.note: The one `isTauri()` here decides whether an interactive approval is needed at all, and that is not a capability question. ADR-0162 puts the approval on the two transfer opens so a REMOTE device asks a human at the host; the desktop is that host, so there is nobody else to ask and a lease would be a permission with no grantor. Every other call in this module is transport-neutral and reaches the same implementation through `invoke` or `_rpc`.

lib/shell-intelligence.note: shell-job-run `defaultCanLongPoll()` is `isTauri() && !isRemoteHostActive()` because `background_job_wait` is classified `client` and never follows a remote host; elsewhere it sleep-polls. The jobs supervisor (cognia_jobs) is host-neutral; reclassifying the wait as execution removes the guard.

lib/signaling.note: desktop-controller.ts is a documented no-op off Tauri; the mobile mirror lives in transport-rtc.ts.

lib/support-report.note: Two guards: `clipboardAvailable()` probes the host so the copy button is never a silent no-op (legitimate), and the `crashReports` section declares `isAvailable: () => isTauri()`. A headless server produces native crash reports too, so that section is gated to the desktop by omission rather than by a physical boundary.

lib/tauri.note: 121 guards — the transport seam itself. `pickTransport()` choosing Tauri/Companion/WebStub per host is the mechanism parity rests on, not a gap in it.

lib/tauri/glance.ts.note: Inter-window channel between the desktop main window and its tray-panel/pet/island/dock webviews (ADR-0225 §7). Every event is sent with `emitTo(windowLabel)` because those windows share one root layout; Transport has no emit and no window addressing, and a headless host has no second window. The phone glance travels on lib/glance/remote/. Same footing as lib/island and lib/usage-dock.

lib/terminal.note: headless holds the `pty` capability and ws_terminal.rs already proxies real PTY frames over WS and WebRTC; pick-transport.ts still returns "unsupported" for anything that is not Tauri/Capacitor/remote-host.

lib/tray.note: OS tray needs a desktop session.

lib/tts.note: Synthesis is host-neutral; local audio playback may not be.

lib/updates.note: runtime restricts browser-extension and CLI update adapters to Tauri, while desktop/mobile installers have separate adapters. CLI presence and updates can also exist on a headless execution host; that adapter support still needs capability-based selection.

lib/usage-dock.note: OS overlay window (ADR-0165 Phase 2). The Capacity Dock is a second Tauri window, label "usage-dock", opened from the main window and driven from inside itself. The nine guards in lib/usage-dock/client.ts are what let the browser and mobile shells import the module without a guard at every call site; a host with no second window to place has nothing to migrate here.

lib/vector.note: Native sqlite-vec throws a typed unsupported-platform error off-Tauri; cloud backends work anywhere.

packages/agent-config-types.note: The only guard token is documentation in the settings-sync contract explaining why machine-local wallpaper refs cannot cross hosts; no runtime branch exists in this package.

automation_audit_snapshot.reason: Reads the local desktop AutomationState audit trail of OS input automation. There is no OS automation engine or corresponding audit state on a headless host.

automation_kill_switch.reason: Stops the local desktop automation engine via kill_switch::engage and AppHandle, including pending OS input and desktop consent. A remote device may halt its paired desktop, but a headless host has no such engine.

automation_kill_switch_engaged.reason: Reads the desktop OS automation emergency-stop gate. Returning false on a headless host would invent the state of an engine that does not exist there.

automation_settings_get.reason: Reads the desktop AutomationState permission gate for accessibility/input automation. Headless hosts have no desktop automation permission surface to configure.
